what: THE GUARANTEED BASELINE. Ours, shipped with the SDK, and not the customer's to change. Every rule here is software-enforceable or it would not be in the file: each names an internal check the SDK ships, so it holds on any machine, in any repo, without the customer configuring anything.

rules.title: A verdict is never green without having run a check
rules.why: The single failure this product exists to catch: 'every contract holds' printed by something that checked nothing. Two things that pass while being wrong were found this way (zero gates; a check that was red anyway).

rules.title: Every proof names a real file in the repo
rules.why: A proof whose guard cannot be pointed at is a row about nothing — a name in a comment counted as evidence until an independent review broke it.

rules.title: A guard is only accepted if its check passes clean and fails when sabotaged
rules.why: An always-red check reads as 'caught' while proving nothing. A gate nobody has seen go both ways is a hope.

rules.title: This file's hash matches what the SDK shipped
rules.why: A baseline a customer can edit is not a guarantee. Editing it locally must be detectable, not merely discouraged.

rules.title: Every unenforced rule is counted, never silently ignored
rules.why: A rule with no check is an opinion. It may be accepted, but the count is printed on every run so 'we adopted the SOPs' cannot hide the ones nothing enforces.

rules.title: The run leaves a record a stranger could re-check
rules.why: Morpheus's doctrine: a verdict that exists only in a terminal is not evidence. mutations.json, the report and the hash are written down.
